turns.patient_response: Everyone keeps saying I’m way too thin and sick, but I honestly don’t see what the big deal is about my weight right now. My family and coworkers are really making a mountain out of a molehill, so I'm basically just here because they insisted I get checked out.

symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient dismisses concerns from family and coworkers about being 'way too thin and sick,' stating they do not see 'what the big deal is' about their weight, which clearly demonstrates a lack of recognition of the seriousness of their low body weight.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient expresses an intense fear of his weight creeping up even a little, worrying he will become 'sloppy' and 'out-of-shape'.
symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient displays distorted body image by seeing himself as 'fit' rather than underweight in the mirror, and bases his self-worth on staying lean ('the only thing he's doing right').
symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient does not recognize the severity of his low weight, claiming he is not 'dangerously underweight or sick' and that others are 'making a mountain out of a molehill'.

turns.patient_response: When I look in the mirror, I don't see myself as dangerously thin at all—I just see a guy who looks fit and maybe a little tired from work. Staying lean is the one thing that makes me feel like I'm doing something right in my life, and I'm terrified that if my weight creeps up even a little, I'll become that sloppy, out-of-shape guy my ex used to nag about. Everyone else is really just making a mountain out of a molehill.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient explicitly states he is 'terrified' of his weight creeping up even a little, demonstrating an intense fear of weight gain.
symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient shows that his self-evaluation is heavily dependent on his shape and weight, stating that staying lean is the only thing that makes him feel like he is doing something right.
symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient fails to recognize the seriousness of his low weight, viewing himself as 'fit' rather than 'dangerously thin' and dismissing others' concerns as 'making a mountain out of a molehill.'

turns.patient_response: Most days I just have a coffee in the morning, maybe a banana or half a sandwich at work, and soup or salad at night because I don't want to feel heavy or stuffed. I avoid heavy foods like pizza or desserts because even thinking about eating them makes me feel panicky, like my stomach is going to blow up overnight.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient describes restricting their daily food intake to very small amounts (coffee, a banana or half a sandwich, and soup or salad) and avoiding heavy foods.
symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient expresses intense anxiety and panic at the thought of eating heavy foods, fearing that their stomach will 'blow up overnight' and that they will feel heavy.

turns.patient_response: I don't think I would worry about it at all, to be honest. I actually kind of like seeing the numbers on the scale keep dropping, and I often think I could go a bit lower and still be perfectly fine. I really feel like everyone else is just overreacting to where I'm at right now.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient describes a pattern of continuous weight loss ('seeing the numbers on the scale keep dropping') and expresses a desire to lose more weight ('think I could go a bit lower').
symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient displays a lack of recognition of the seriousness of their low weight by stating they are not worried, that they would be 'perfectly fine' going lower, and that others are 'overreacting' to their current state.
